title: Bagging Streams and Roll-Off Loads for Mold Remediation Debris
content:
Supervisor's guide to Mold Remediation debris loads. The drywall removed square feet are the total quantity of the drywall removal lines booked on the job, and the insulation removed square feet the total quantity of its insulation removal lines.

**Load count.**

- A job with both drywall and insulation removal lines bags them as separate streams, and its loads are the drywall removed square feet divided by the drywall load capacity of 160 square feet, rounded up to a whole load, plus the insulation removed square feet divided by the insulation load capacity of 120 square feet, rounded up to a whole load.
- A job with drywall removal lines only, whose drywall removed square feet are above the roll-off threshold of 400 square feet, is hauled in a roll-off priced at no fewer than the roll-off minimum of 4 loads, and its loads are the larger of two load counts: 4, and the quotient of the drywall removed square feet divided by 160, rounded up to a whole load.
- Every other job's loads are the drywall and insulation removed square feet together divided by the drywall load capacity of 160 square feet, rounded up to a whole load.

| Hypothetical removal | Loads |
|---|---|
| Drywall 330 sq ft and insulation 130 sq ft | 3 plus 2, which is 5 |
| Drywall 450 sq ft only | The larger of 4 and 3, which is 4 |
| Drywall 700 sq ft only | The larger of 4 and 5, which is 5 |
| Drywall 400 sq ft only | Not above 400: 400 divided by 160 rounded up, which is 3 |
| Insulation 250 sq ft only | 250 divided by 160 rounded up, which is 2 |
